TEXT — edit this column: Three more days, encik. Then I ORD.

Where it appears: Episode 2 · Chapter 5 · The Last Question — The encik, the sergeant-major (episode 2): Play: the small talk
TEXT — edit this column: Good. Go home. Eat properly, sleep properly.

Where it appears: Episode 2 · Chapter 5 · The Last Question — The encik, the sergeant-major (episode 2): Play: the turn — unprompted, halfway through
TEXT — edit this column: Eh. You remember the question you asked me? In the cookhouse. About the three o'clock shower.

Where it appears: Episode 2 · Chapter 5 · The Last Question — James at eighteen (episode 2): The decision, option A
TEXT — edit this column: Who was it, encik? What was his story?

Where it appears: Episode 2 · Chapter 5 · The Last Question — James at eighteen (episode 2): The decision, option B
TEXT — edit this column: I don't think about it anymore, encik.

Where it appears: Episode 2 · Chapter 5 · The Last Question — James at eighteen (episode 2): The decision, option C
TEXT — edit this column: I think I was just too stressed.

Where it appears: Episode 2 · Chapter 5 · The Last Question — James at eighteen (episode 2): The decision, option D
TEXT — edit this column: Why didn't you tell me then, encik?

Where it appears: Episode 2 · Chapter 5 · The Last Question — The encik, the sergeant-major (episode 2): Scene A: the recruit in bed one
TEXT — edit this column: Before my time. One recruit, bed one. Quiet boy. Every night he's the last one in the shower. He don't like people see him wash.

Where it appears: Episode 2 · Chapter 5 · The Last Question — The encik, the sergeant-major (episode 2): Scene A: the morning they found him
TEXT — edit this column: One morning, first parade, he's not there. They find him inside. Water still running.

Where it appears: Episode 2 · Chapter 5 · The Last Question — The encik, the sergeant-major (episode 2): Scene A: after
TEXT — edit this column: No note. No reason. His family come and take him back. The bunk close for one month. Then they open it again like nothing.

Where it appears: Episode 2 · Chapter 5 · The Last Question — The encik, the sergeant-major (episode 2): Scene A: the attachment line — the episode's teaching
TEXT — edit this column: Since then, every batch, bed one, three o'clock. Sometimes the departed are still stuck at the places they have attachments to. That shower was his.

Where it appears: Episode 2 · Chapter 5 · The Last Question — The encik, the sergeant-major (episode 2): Scene A: and he closes it
TEXT — edit this column: You asked, so I told you. But don't go and make it into something. He's not your business.

Where it appears: Episode 2 · Chapter 5 · The Last Question — The encik, the sergeant-major (episode 2): Scene B: the nod
TEXT — edit this column: Good. Better than me.

Where it appears: Episode 2 · Chapter 5 · The Last Question — The encik, the sergeant-major (episode 2): Scene B: his own night in that bunk
TEXT — edit this column: I was in that bunk also. I went to look once. Water running. Somebody standing under it, back facing me. I went back to bed and never look again. One month, then nothing.

Where it appears: Episode 2 · Chapter 5 · The Last Question — The encik, the sergeant-major (episode 2): Scene B: why he said nothing in the cookhouse
TEXT — edit this column: That morning in the cookhouse I say nothing, because if I tell you, you check every night until ORD. You didn't.

Where it appears: Episode 2 · Chapter 5 · The Last Question — The encik, the sergeant-major (episode 2): Scene B: the line that closes the episode
TEXT — edit this column: After your batch posted out. Quiet. First time in years.

Where it appears: Episode 2 · Chapter 5 · The Last Question — The encik, the sergeant-major (episode 2): Scene C: the whole scene
TEXT — edit this column: I know it is easier to brush things off with logic and reason. But there are many things you simply won't fully understand.

Where it appears: Episode 2 · Chapter 5 · The Last Question — The encik, the sergeant-major (episode 2): Scene D: the boy he told once
TEXT — edit this column: Because I told one boy before you. Same question. After that he checked every night. Two months later he's out. Not sick. Not injured. Just cannot anymore.

Where it appears: Episode 2 · Chapter 5 · The Last Question — The encik, the sergeant-major (episode 2): Scene D: the rule he made after
TEXT — edit this column: After him I decide. Nobody gets told until they are leaving.

Where it appears: Episode 2 · Chapter 5 · The Last Question — The encik, the sergeant-major (episode 2): Scene D: and the quiet
TEXT — edit this column: After your batch posted out. Quiet. First time in years. Now you know. Now it cannot hurt you.

Where it appears: Episode 2 · Chapter 5 · The Last Question — James at eighteen (episode 2): Under outcome card A
TEXT — edit this column: I asked who he was. Encik told me, and then told me to leave it there.

Where it appears: Episode 2 · Chapter 5 · The Last Question — James at eighteen (episode 2): Under outcome card B
TEXT — edit this column: I had already let it go. He only confirmed I was right to.

Where it appears: Episode 2 · Chapter 5 · The Last Question — James at eighteen (episode 2): Under outcome card C
TEXT — edit this column: I called it stress. He wouldn't let me.

Where it appears: Episode 2 · Chapter 5 · The Last Question — James at eighteen (episode 2): Under outcome card D
TEXT — edit this column: I wanted a reason I was owed. He gave me one. It didn't help.

Where it appears: Episode 2 · Chapter 5 · The Last Question — James at eighteen (episode 2): The closing narration, to camera, in all four outcomes
TEXT — edit this column: The departed stay where their attachments are. So do the living. His was that shower. Mine was the question. When I put it down, so did he.
